questions.statement: My brother ___ TV right now. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: A friend is watching TV at this exact moment.

options.feedback: Is watching is the present continuous: the action is happening at this moment.
Watches is present simple, used for habits and fixed facts, not for an action in progress.
Watch has no auxiliary verb, so it cannot form the progressive.
Is watch is wrong because the progressive needs the -ing form after the auxiliary.

questions.explanation:
The present continuous is auxiliary to be plus the -ing form: is watching. It describes an action in progress at the moment of speaking.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: They ___ to Madrid every summer. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: A family habit that repeats every summer.

options.feedback: Are going is the present continuous, which needs a temporary situation, not a yearly habit.
Go is present simple, the tense used for a repeated seasonal habit.
Goes agrees with he, she or it only, while the subject here is they.
Is going also disagrees with the plural subject they.

questions.explanation:
Every summer marks a habit that repeats year after year, so the present simple is the right tense: they go.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Look! It ___ outside. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: You look out of the window and see the rain falling right now.

options.feedback: Rains is present simple; here the rain is visible happening at this moment.
Rain is the bare infinitive, which cannot stand as the verb of this sentence.
Is raining is the present continuous, and Look signals an action in progress.
Has rained is present perfect and points to a period that is already over.

questions.explanation:
Look at the window is evidence of an action happening now, so the present continuous is correct: it is raining.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: ___ your sister working at the moment? Choose the correct auxiliary.
questions.context: You want to know what your sister is doing these seconds.

options.feedback: Are agrees with you, we, they or a plural subject, but your sister is singular.
Do builds the present simple and cannot be followed by working.
Does also builds the present simple and cannot be followed by an -ing form.
Is agrees with the third person singular subject your sister and with the -ing form working.

questions.explanation:
The present continuous question uses the auxiliary be followed by the subject, then the -ing form: Is your sister working?
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The baby ___ in the next room while I was reading. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: A loud noise interrupted your reading this morning.

options.feedback: Was crying was continuous past, and it keeps the explanation of the noise in the past.
Is crying is present continuous and would place the noise in the present moment.
Cries is present simple, a general fact that does not describe the single past moment.
Has cried is present perfect and stresses a result in the present instead of the past scene.

questions.explanation:
The noise and the reading both belong to a past period that was in progress, so the past continuous is the right choice: was crying.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: While she ___, the phone rang. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: Two actions in the same past moment.

options.feedback: Is cooking is present continuous and does not fit a past story.
Was cooking is the past continuous used as the longer background action of a past period.
Cooks is present simple, which cannot introduce the background of a past event.
Will cook belongs to the future and has no place in a past narrative.

questions.explanation:
The past continuous sets the scene: a longer action in progress when another past event interrupted it, so she was cooking.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: You want to correct someone who said that water boils at 100 degrees as a permanent fact.

options.feedback: Is boiling is the present continuous, used for an action in progress, not for a general scientific fact.
Boiled is past simple and would date the fact to a finished past moment.
Boils is present simple, the tense that expresses a general or permanent truth.
Was boiling is past continuous and would describe a temporary past situation.

questions.explanation:
A scientific law is a general truth, so the present simple is the tense the language uses: water boils at 100 degrees.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What do you do? I ___ swimming every Saturday. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: You meet a friend who asks what you do in your free time.

options.feedback: Am swimming is the present continuous and would imply the action happens only now.
Swims agrees with he, she or it, but the subject here is I.
Was swimming is past continuous and describes an unfinished past routine.
Swim is present simple, correct for a routine repeated every week.

questions.explanation:
Every Saturday is a repeated habit, and habits take the present simple: I swim.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the sentence that describes an action in progress right now.
questions.context: Two people describe the same morning in different words.

options.text: She is reading a novel at the moment.
options.feedback: Is reading at the moment is present continuous and places the action exactly now.
Reads every night is present simple and describes a repeated habit.

options.text: She read a novel last night.
options.feedback: Read last night is past simple and refers to a finished past action.

options.text: She will read a novel tomorrow.
options.feedback: Will read is future simple and belongs to tomorrow.

questions.explanation:
At the moment is the clearest marker of the present continuous: an action happening now, so she is reading.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Usually I walk to school, but today I ___ the bus. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: A contrast between a permanent condition and a temporary action.

options.feedback: Take is present simple and would describe the usual habit, not the exception of today.
Am taking is the present continuous used for a temporary change from the normal routine.
Takes agrees with he, she or it only, while the subject here is I.
Was taking is past continuous and would place the exception in the past.

questions.explanation:
But today marks a temporary deviation from a habit, and temporary present situations take the present continuous: I am taking the bus.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: ___ you mind opening the window? Choose the correct auxiliary.
questions.context: A hotel receptionist answering a polite request.

options.feedback: Do builds the present simple and cannot be followed by the -ing form opening.
Does also builds the present simple and does not fit this structure.
Are is the auxiliary of the present continuous and belongs to the polite structure Do you mind opening.
Did is the past auxiliary and would place the request in the past.

questions.explanation:
In Do you mind opening the window, the mind clause carries the auxiliary do and the verb appears in the -ing form, so the opening part uses are.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the sentence in which the tense is correct.
questions.context: You are correcting a classmate who chose the wrong tense.

options.text: At eight o'clock I am have breakfast every day.
options.feedback: Am have mixes the two present forms and produces a form that does not exist in English.

options.text: At eight o'clock I having breakfast.
options.feedback: Having cannot stand alone as the verb; it needs an auxiliary such as is having.

options.text: At eight o'clock I has breakfast.
options.feedback: Has agrees with he, she or it, but the subject here is I.

options.text: At eight o'clock I have breakfast every day.
options.feedback: Have is present simple, the tense a daily routine with a fixed hour requires.

questions.explanation:
A routine with a fixed hour is present simple: at eight o'clock I have breakfast every day. Every day removes any doubt about the tense.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: She ___ to music now; she never does it in the morning. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: A negative statement about what is happening at this moment.

options.feedback: Is not listening is the present continuous in the negative, needed for the temporary action happening now.
Does not listen is the negative present simple, used for habits and facts.
Not listens leaves the sentence without an auxiliary and is not a valid form.
Is listen is wrong because the progressive requires the -ing form listening.

questions.explanation:
Now calls for the present continuous in the negative form, so the sentence needs is not listening.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: I am not tired. ___ I? Choose the correct question tag.
questions.context: A speaker wants to say the opposite of what he just said.

options.feedback: Don't you would require a present simple statement such as I am not tired never appears with do.
Aren't you is the tag that matches the statement I am not tired: plural you with the negative auxiliary are.
Isn't you mixes the singular is with the plural pronoun you.
Aren't I would question the speaker instead of the listener, which the comma demands you to do.

questions.explanation:
A negative statement with I takes the tag aren't you, because the tag is built from the auxiliary and you of the sentence.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Hurry up! The train ___. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: A short action that is happening as you write this.

options.feedback: Leaves is present simple and would describe a scheduled habit, not this urgent moment.
Left is past simple and would place the departure in a finished past moment.
Is leaving is the present continuous and expresses the departure as a situation in progress now.
Will leave is future simple, while the train is about to go in the present situation.

questions.explanation:
Hurry up signals an urgent present situation, so the departure is expressed with the present continuous: the train is leaving.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the option that correctly combines the two present forms.
questions.context: A summary of a week for a school report.

options.text: He usually is walking, but today he walks to the exam.
options.feedback: Usually is walking reverses the roles of the two forms and turns the habit into a permanent action.

options.text: He usually walks, but today he walks to the exam.
options.feedback: Both clauses would be present simple and would hide the temporary change of today.

options.text: He usually walking, but today he is walking to the exam.
options.feedback: Usually walking has no auxiliary and cannot build the first half of the sentence.

options.text: He usually walks, but today he is walking to the exam.
options.feedback: Usually walks gives the present simple for the habit and today he is walking the present continuous for the exception.

questions.explanation:
The contrast between a permanent habit and a temporary change is the classic pairing of present simple and present continuous, exactly as the correct option shows.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: He ___ his bicycle because the chain is broken. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: You watch your friend through the window and describe the scene.

options.feedback: Is repairing is the present continuous and describes the repair happening while you watch.
Repairs is present simple, used for routines and repeated jobs.
Repair is the bare infinitive and cannot be the verb of this sentence alone.
Is repair is not a valid form, because the progressive needs the -ing form.

questions.explanation:
You can see the action in progress, which is exactly what the present continuous describes: he is repairing his bicycle.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The sun ___ in the east. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: A fact that is true in this country.

options.feedback: Is rising is present continuous and would need a specific moment of observation.
Rises is present simple, the tense used for a permanent and general fact.
Rose is past simple and would tell us when the sun rose this morning.
Was rising is past continuous and belongs to a description of the past.

questions.explanation:
A daily natural fact is expressed with the present simple: the sun rises in the east.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: I ___ here for three weeks and I still have not seen the cathedral. Choose the correct form.
questions.context: A tourist tells you what she is doing during her stay.

options.feedback: Stay is present simple and would describe a habit rather than a temporary visit.
Stayed is past simple and would end the stay before the second clause.
Am staying is the present continuous used for a temporary situation that lasts during the stay.
Was staying is past continuous, but the visit is still not finished.

questions.explanation:
For three weeks describes a temporary period that is still open, and that is what the present continuous expresses: I am staying here.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the sentence that is correct.
questions.context: A short dialogue in which a speaker announces a new plan.

options.text: I meeting my cousin at six.
options.feedback: Meeting has no auxiliary, so the sentence has no verb in the present continuous.

options.text: I meet my cousin at six o'clock yesterday.
options.feedback: Yesterday forces the past, which makes meet impossible in that position.

options.text: I am meet my cousin at six.
options.feedback: Am meet repeats the auxiliary and lacks the -ing form the progressive requires.

options.text: I am meeting my cousin at six.
options.feedback: Am meeting is a valid present continuous sentence announcing a fixed arrangement.

questions.explanation:
Present continuous arrangements take be plus the -ing form, so I am meeting my cousin at six is the only well-formed option.
---
questions.subject: ingles
